name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:fix. Changelog (last 3): 7.320.0 — The mocks provenance ledger is deleted end to end (grammar, gate, confirmation round, counts line, exclusion rows, roadmap parking-lot check and the mocks-ledger template); the scaffold tournament's race-or-skip question becomes an auto-picked skip with a veto; the roadmap brief drops its unread Risk, Design stage, Lane and Expected specs fields and the genesis brief its duplicate Journeys section; ops-ADR derive and coverage passes and the mocks legacy-status edge paragraphs are removed. 7.319.0 — fanout-driver: a red main gate now outranks DISPATCH, so the next planned lane is never dispatched onto a red main after --mark merged (a pending question still relays first); --mark gate-repaired re-loads the state after the long gate run and applies only its outcome, so a --mark returned that landed meanwhile is no longer clobbered; merging a fix lane with a queueId ticks its queue item through spec-queue done (whatever the gate colour, since the work is on main), warning instead of dying when the tick fails; and a green gate-repaired drops that lane's 'main gate red' line from the queued list, so the report no longer lists a repair that no longer exists. 7.318.0 — fix(review): finishMerge keeps the review state where the merge-strategy mark finds it until merge-back.sh cleanup exits 0, and cleanup lifts the agent harness's own 'claude agent' worktree lock — a failed close cleanup is re-runnable.
